currentContext.business: TCI operates a comprehensive multimodal logistics portfolio built around three main activities: Freight Transport (organised surface transport covering FTL, LTL, over-dimensional cargo and project heavy haul across India and SAARC/BBIN nations), Supply Chain Solutions (a single-window enabler covering network design, inventory management, modern warehousing and multimodal transportation from 'conceptualization to implementation'), and Coastal Transportation (multimodal coastal shipping connecting India's western, eastern and southern ports with first- and last-mile rail and road connectivity). Execution is supported by an asset-backed network — vehicles, warehousing, yards, hubs and branches — and a digital backbone of proprietary Transportation and Warehouse Management Systems, control towers and AI/ML-driven route and network optimisation. Customers span automotive, chemicals, engineering, retail, e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, FMCG, consumer durables and defence.

Coastal Transportation: First and last mile connectivity via rail and road

on the Company's website, and dividends are recommended with reference to that policy; for FY26 the AGM notice puts a final dividend of Rs 1 per equity share of face value Rs 2 each to shareholders for declaration. The Company funds itself without public deposits — it has not accepted any deposit within the meaning of Sections 73 and 74 of the Companies Act during the year. Beyond distributions, the Company's stated intent is long-term value creation through sound governance: the Audit Committee scrutinises inter-corporate loans and investments, reviews utilisation of funds raised through issuances and statements of deviation, approves and monitors related party transactions, and considers schemes such as mergers, demergers and amalgamations. Social spend is channelled through its CSR arm, TCI Foundation, under a Board-approved CSR Policy.|Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) framework across operations, with PPE provision, regular safety training and awareness programmes for drivers and employees, and stringent safety protocols for cargo handling and transportation|24x7 GPS-enabled fleet monitoring through centralised control towers to enhance road safety and operational oversight|TCI Safe Safar initiative promoting health, safety and responsible driving practices among truck drivers and the broader transport community|Employee welfare supported through medical and insurance coverage; retention supported through structured learning and development, upskilling/reskilling, leadership development, ESOPs and a robust grievance redressal mechanism|Climate change formally identified as a material responsible-business-conduct risk in the BRSR, on the basis of disruption from extreme weather events such as cyclones, heat waves and floods|Corporate governance, board oversight, ethics, risk management and compliance identified in the BRSR as a material issue with positive financial implications, backed by a Board-level governance framework, internal controls, compliance management and enterprise risk management processes|Multimodal shift as the Company's stated decarbonisation lever — greater adoption of rail and coastal transportation to lower carbon intensity and improve fuel efficiency (MD&A/Chairman narrative; no quantified emissions target is disclosed in the routed sections)|BRSR reporting boundary is standalone and no assurance was obtained (name and type of assurance provider both stated as 'Not Applicable'), so the sustainability disclosures are unassured and exclude subsidiaries|Permanent-employee attrition disclosed at 8.73% total for FY 2025-26 (8.55% male, 13.65% female), improved from 9.88% in FY 2024-25; women represent 3.40% of total employees, 20% of the Board of Directors and 12.50% of KMPs|CSR delivered through TCI Foundation in healthcare, education, sports, community development, skill development, employment generation and environment protection
currentContext.expansion: The routed sections carry no rupee capex plan, no named project with a commissioning date and no capacity-addition schedule; expansion is described qualitatively as footprint and capability build-out. The Chairman states that during the year the Company "continued to invest in strategic priorities including multimodal infrastructure, technology integra[tion]", while the Board's Report explicitly records that "there have been no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of this report". The existing asset footprint against which expansion is framed comprises 17 Mn. sq. ft. of warehousing space (dry and temperature controlled) with modern storage systems (RFID, ASRS, Pick/Put to Light), 67 yards managed across India, 4,500+ vehicles under operation of which 1,350+ are owned, and 180+ trains operated per month. Forward-looking capability expansion is stated at the divisional level for TCI Supply Chain Solutions: expansion of integrated 3PL and LLP service offerings, network optimisation and multimodal logistics capabilities, strategically located warehousing including temperature-controlled infrastructure, scalable storage solutions aligned with dynamic demand patterns, optimised network design for improved connectivity, and warehouse capacity gains via advanced design and vertical space optimization rather than footprint alone. The only capital-structure change disclosed for the year is the allotment of 135,035 equity shares on exercise of ESOP 2017 tranches 5, 6 and 7, taking the equity share count from 76,608,762 to 76,743,797 shares.
currentContext.mdna: India's economic formalisation is accelerating — GST collections rising and e-way bill volumes up 21% — translating directly into higher velocity and demand for integrated logistics|Modal rebalancing: commissioning of 96.4% of Dedicated Freight Corridors is driving a decisive shift from road to rail, enhancing cost-efficiency for long-haul freight|Structural shift from fragmented services to end-to-end, integrated, tech-enabled supply chains, with rising 4PL demand (~12% CAGR) reflecting a market-wide pivot to single-window outsourced logistics management|Manufacturing integration: PLI schemes have catalysed over Rs 2.0 lakh crore of investment, requiring high-capacity multimodal logistics connecting factory zones to export hubs|The EU–India FTA opening new export corridors in autos, pharma and advanced manufacturing, deepening India's integration with global value chains|Climate-conscious trade rules and sustainability expectations making low-carbon, multimodal movement a necessity rather than an advantage|Warehousing utilisation remained strong during the year, supported by manufacturing expansion and consumption-led demand; rail operations enhanced long-haul efficiency and network productivity; coastal shipping continued to scale with growing multimodal adoption|Cold chain capabilities strengthened presence across pharmaceuticals, food and quick-commerce sectors|Growth of e-commerce and quick commerce redefining warehousing strategy toward distributed networks, faster turnaround and efficient inventory positioning|Digitalisation has moved from differentiator to baseline — ULIP has crossed 100 crore API transactions and India's logistics cost has reached ~7.97% of GDP — so operators without embedded technology operate at a structural disadvantage|Sector consolidation and technology-led transformation, where TCI's scale, experience and execution capability are described as a competitive advantage|Geopolitical volatility as a counterweight: the US-Israel and Iran conflict escalating since February 2026 has hit maritime choke points including the Strait of Hormuz, cut global air cargo capacity by approximately 18%, and spiked bunker fuel prices and war-risk surcharges

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety across long-haul transport, warehousing and hazardous-cargo handling
risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Given operations in long-distance transportation, warehousing, cargo handling and movement of diverse consignments including hazardous and chemical goods, road accidents, driver fatigue, workplace incidents and health-related risks may adversely impact employees, business continuity, operational efficiency and stakeholder confidence. Mitigation is an EHS framework with PPE, driver and employee safety training, stringent cargo-handling protocols, 24x7 GPS-enabled fleet monitoring through centralised control towers, medical/insurance cover and the TCI Safe Safar driver initiative.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: inability to attract, develop and retain skilled talent may impact operational efficiency, service quality, productivity and the Company's ability to meet customer expectations and growth objectives. Mitigated through structured learning and development, job rotation, upskilling/reskilling, leadership development, performance-based progression, recognition programmes, ESOPs and academic/industry partnerships for a talent pipeline.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications — worldwide businesses have reported newer and emerging cybersecurity threats such as ransomware, posing risk to everyday business operations. The Company states it has adequate cyber and IT security systems including ITDR, verified by external consultants with all recommendations implemented. Exposure is structurally rising as operations become dependent on proprietary TMS/WMS, control towers and digital documentation.

risks.risk: Climate change and extreme weather disruption
risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: climate change can impact operations through extreme weather events such as cyclones, heat waves and floods, which have the potential to create severe disruptions to a pan-India road, rail and coastal network (the mitigation text is truncated in the routed source).

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to trade lanes, energy and freight costs
risks.note: The MD&A records that the US-Israel and Iran conflict, escalating since February 2026, has hit critical maritime choke points including the Strait of Hormuz, forcing vessel rerouting, suspended operations and a surge in war-risk surcharges and insurance premiums; Gulf airspace closures cut global air cargo capacity by approximately 18%; and energy-market volatility spiked bunker fuel prices, creating cascading cost pressure across supply chains. Coastal shipping and cross-border operations sit directly in this exposure.

risks.risk: Structural dependence on a contract/outsourced workforce
risks.note: The BRSR workforce table shows Nil permanent workers against 8,904 workers who are 'other than permanent', alongside 4,165 permanent employees. Service quality, safety compliance and cost are therefore delivered largely through a non-permanent workforce and vendor/driver ecosystem the Company does not employ directly.

Exports contribute only 0.18% of total turnover and international presence is limited to three countries (Bangladesh, Nepal, UAE) with no international offices reported in the BRSR operations table, so earnings are tied almost entirely to Indian freight, warehousing and coastal demand cycles despite the Company's stated global-connectivity ambition.

risks.risk: Competitive/technology displacement as digitalisation becomes the baseline
risks.note: The MD&A states that logistics digitalisation has shifted from a competitive advantage to a fundamental operational requirement and that organisations failing to embed technology into core workflows now operate at a structural disadvantage, with ~70% of logistics enterprises accelerating digital transformation — implying continuous, non-discretionary technology spend simply to hold position.

The BRSR transparency table reports 3,238 customer complaints filed in FY 2025-26 (figures reworked to include all major and material complaints), handled through a toll-free number, email and an escalation matrix — a scale-driven service-quality watch item in a business whose differentiation is stated to be reliability and visibility.

one-line thesis: TCIL is leveraging digital integration and strategic capacity expansion in high-margin segments like cold chain and coastal shipping to offset weak FTL/LTL freight demand, maintaining consistent top-line growth and net-debt-free balance sheet while building moats through end-to-end solutions for premium clients like Japanese FMCG firms.

capital allocation: Net debt free; ₹160cr buyback completed; dividend payout ratio increased to 175% (from 125%); cash reserves ₹280cr; Capex funded via internal accruals and low-cost truck debt; no external fund-raise planned
risks & watch-items: LTL freight price wars from listed competitors; MSME credit slowdown impacting freight volumes; geopolitical volatility affecting shipping rates; margin compression from new warehousing investments; delayed second-hand ship acquisition; regulatory delays in coastal shipping incentives
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; acknowledges headwinds in freight but emphasizes resilience through diversification; highlights digital moats (ULIP APIs), customer retention via quality (e.g., Japanese food case), and long-term capacity building; avoids over-promising on Seaways margins; cautious on near-term FTL recovery
non-obvious takeaways: TCIL's ULIP API integration (Vahan, FASTag, FIOS) is a unique, industry-leading digital moat not replicated by competitors; cold chain and quick commerce fulfillment are not just revenue streams but data-rich platforms for future value extraction; the company's branch network expansion (32 new) is a stealth advantage for last-mile penetration in unorganized logistics markets

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

hero.oneLiner: Transport Corporation of India (TCI) is a six-decade-old integrated multimodal logistics provider that positions itself as a single-window partner across road, rail, coastal shipping, warehousing and supply chain solutions, and states it moves cargo equal to nearly 2% of India's GDP by value.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Transport Corporation of India (TCI) is a six-decade-old integrated multimodal logistics provider that positions itself as a single-window partner across road, rail, coastal shipping, warehousing and supply chain solutions, and states it moves cargo equal to nearly 2% of India's GDP by value.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: TCI operates a comprehensive multimodal logistics portfolio built around three main activities: Freight Transport (organised surface transport covering FTL, LTL, over-dimensional cargo and project heavy haul across India and SAARC/BBIN nations), Supply Chain Solutions (a single-window enabler covering network design, inventory management, modern warehousing and multimodal transportation from 'conceptualization to implementation'), and Coastal Transportation (multimodal coastal shipping connecting India's western, eastern and southern ports with first- and last-mile rail and road connectivity). Execution is supported by an asset-backed network — vehicles, warehousing, yards, hubs and branches — and a digital backbone of proprietary Transportation and Warehouse Management Systems, control towers and AI/ML-driven route and network optimisation. Customers span automotive, chemicals, engineering, retail, e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, FMCG, consumer durables and defence.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- TCI-CONCOR Multimodal Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — subsidiary: 51% held by the Company; multimodal solutions; classified as a material subsidiary based on the financial statements as at March 31, 2026
- TCI Cold Chain Solutions Ltd. — subsidiary: 80% held by the Company; cold chain logistics
- TCI Chemlog Pvt. Ltd. — subsidiary: 100% held by the Company; chemical logistics
- TCI Holdings Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd. — subsidiary: 100% held by the Company; Singapore-incorporated holding entity; sold its 100% stake in TCI Global (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. during the year
- TCI Bangladesh Ltd. — subsidiary: 100% held by the Company; Bangladesh operations
- TCI Nepal Pvt. Ltd. — subsidiary: 100% held by the Company; Nepal operations
- TCIL Middle East Logistics Services L.L.C — subsidiary: 100% held by the Company; Middle East (UAE) logistics services
- TCI Global (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. — subsidiary: Former step-down wholly owned subsidiary; ceased to be a subsidiary as on 26th January 2026 following sale of the 100% stake by its parent TCI Holdings Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd.
- Transystem Logistics International Pvt. Ltd. — JV: Joint venture, 49% held by the Company; latest audited balance sheet date 31st March 2026
- Cargo Exchange India Pvt. Ltd. — associate: Associate, 32.50% held by the Company (shown in Form AOC-1 Part B as Cargo Exchange Pvt. Ltd., latest audited balance sheet 31st March 2025)
- Container Corporation of India Ltd. — related party: Counterparty to material related party transactions with the Company's subsidiary TCI-CONCOR Multimodal Solutions Pvt. Ltd., approved by shareholders under Regulation 23 of the SEBI Listing Regulations
- TCI Foundation — related party: The Company's CSR arm, through which it undertakes healthcare, education, sports, community development, skill development, employment generation and environment protection initiatives

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Freight: 6% growth, margins pressured by LTL competition and cost inflation; Seaways: 22% revenue growth, 40%+ EBITDA margins due to capacity constraints; Supply Chain: 12% growth, H1 revenue ₹800cr, poised to surpass freight by FY26; Cold Chain: 32% growth, 75 new trucks added, major storage expansion underway; Quick Commerce: Fulfillment-only model, no last-mile, learning phase with steady growth; Chemical Logistics: Emerging high-compliance segment with JV potential

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Freight Transport (TCI Freight):** Less than Truck Load (LTL), Full Truck Load (FTL), Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC), Project & Heavy Haul (PHH), Storage Solutions, Cross Border Logistics Solutions (Nepal, Bangladesh), CHA Facility (Customs House Agent services)
- **Supply Chain Solutions (TCI SCS):** Inbound & Outbound Logistics (IBL/OBL) Customization, Warehouse Planning & Management (including vertical space optimization), Yard Management, Supply Chain Design & Reengineering, Lead Logistics Provider (LLP/3PL/4PL), Full-Stack Solution: Conceptualization to Execution, Inventory Management via WMS integrated with client ERP, Proprietary TMS for Route Optimization, Proprietary "Glass Pipeline" supply chain visibility
- **Coastal Transportation:** Coastal shipping, Container cargo movements, First and last mile connectivity via rail and road

growth_optionality.body: Coastal shipping (India's 6% vs China's 20% share); Quick commerce fulfillment (shift from instant to weekly grocery); Chemical logistics (hazardous goods handling); ULIP API ecosystem leadership

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's economic formalisation is accelerating — GST collections rising and e-way bill volumes up 21% — translating directly into higher velocity and demand for integrated logistics
- Modal rebalancing: commissioning of 96.4% of Dedicated Freight Corridors is driving a decisive shift from road to rail, enhancing cost-efficiency for long-haul freight
- Structural shift from fragmented services to end-to-end, integrated, tech-enabled supply chains, with rising 4PL demand (~12% CAGR) reflecting a market-wide pivot to single-window outsourced logistics management
- Manufacturing integration: PLI schemes have catalysed over Rs 2.0 lakh crore of investment, requiring high-capacity multimodal logistics connecting factory zones to export hubs
- The EU–India FTA opening new export corridors in autos, pharma and advanced manufacturing, deepening India's integration with global value chains
- Climate-conscious trade rules and sustainability expectations making low-carbon, multimodal movement a necessity rather than an advantage
- Warehousing utilisation remained strong during the year, supported by manufacturing expansion and consumption-led demand; rail operations enhanced long-haul efficiency and network productivity; coastal shipping continued to scale with growing multimodal adoption
- Cold chain capabilities strengthened presence across pharmaceuticals, food and quick-commerce sectors
- Growth of e-commerce and quick commerce redefining warehousing strategy toward distributed networks, faster turnaround and efficient inventory positioning
- Digitalisation has moved from differentiator to baseline — ULIP has crossed 100 crore API transactions and India's logistics cost has reached ~7.97% of GDP — so operators without embedded technology operate at a structural disadvantage
- Sector consolidation and technology-led transformation, where TCI's scale, experience and execution capability are described as a competitive advantage
- Geopolitical volatility as a counterweight: the US-Israel and Iran conflict escalating since February 2026 has hit maritime choke points including the Strait of Hormuz, cut global air cargo capacity by approximately 18%, and spiked bunker fuel prices and war-risk surcharges

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Freight margins under pressure due to wage inflation, tolls, and price wars from listed LTL players; Cold chain and warehousing margins temporarily compressed due to Capex for new contracts; Seaways margins stable at 40%+ due to capacity crunch; overall EBITDA margin structure resilient

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net debt free; ₹160cr buyback completed; dividend payout ratio increased to 175% (from 125%); cash reserves ₹280cr; Capex funded via internal accruals and low-cost truck debt; no external fund-raise planned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections carry no rupee capex plan, no named project with a commissioning date and no capacity-addition schedule; expansion is described qualitatively as footprint and capability build-out. The Chairman states that during the year the Company "continued to invest in strategic priorities including multimodal infrastructure, technology integra[tion]", while the Board's Report explicitly records that "there have been no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of this report". The existing asset footprint against which expansion is framed comprises 17 Mn. sq. ft. of warehousing space (dry and temperature controlled) with modern storage systems (RFID, ASRS, Pick/Put to Light), 67 yards managed across India, 4,500+ vehicles under operation of which 1,350+ are owned, and 180+ trains operated per month. Forward-looking capability expansion is stated at the divisional level for TCI Supply Chain Solutions: expansion of integrated 3PL and LLP service offerings, network optimisation and multimodal logistics capabilities, strategically located warehousing including temperature-controlled infrastructure, scalable storage solutions aligned with dynamic demand patterns, optimised network design for improved connectivity, and warehouse capacity gains via advanced design and vertical space optimization rather than footprint alone. The only capital-structure change disclosed for the year is the allotment of 135,035 equity shares on exercise of ESOP 2017 tranches 5, 6 and 7, taking the equity share count from 76,608,762 to 76,743,797 shares.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and strategic; acknowledges headwinds in freight but emphasizes resilience through diversification; highlights digital moats (ULIP APIs), customer retention via quality (e.g., Japanese food case), and long-term capacity building; avoids over-promising on Seaways margins; cautious on near-term FTL recovery

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Six decades of operating history in Indian surface logistics; states it moves cargo equal to nearly 2% of India's GDP by value
- Pan-India hub-and-spoke freight network — 25 hubs, 750+ branches, reach across 19,000+ pin codes — plus 1,200+ offices/branches nationally
- Multimodal integration across road, rail, coastal shipping and warehousing on one platform, enabling single-window 3PL/4PL/LLP offerings that customers cannot easily replicate with point providers
- Asset-backed scale: 4,500+ vehicles under operation (1,350+ owned), 180+ trains per month, 17 Mn. sq. ft. of dry and temperature-controlled warehousing and 67 managed yards
- Proprietary technology backbone — TMS for AI-driven route optimisation, WMS integrated with client ERP, centralised control tower and the proprietary "Glass Pipeline" visibility layer
- Deep multi-industry domain expertise across Automotive, Retail, Chemicals, Healthcare, Hi-Tech and Cold Chain
- Cross-border capability into Nepal and Bangladesh with established network, CHA capability with AEO certification and regulatory/customs expertise
- Group ecosystem support — synergistic group company support and TCI Group's wider network feeding TCI SCS execution

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: LTL freight price wars from listed competitors; MSME credit slowdown impacting freight volumes; geopolitical volatility affecting shipping rates; margin compression from new warehousing investments; delayed second-hand ship acquisition; regulatory delays in coastal shipping incentives

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: TCIL's ULIP API integration (Vahan, FASTag, FIOS) is a unique, industry-leading digital moat not replicated by competitors; cold chain and quick commerce fulfillment are not just revenue streams but data-rich platforms for future value extraction; the company's branch network expansion (32 new) is a stealth advantage for last-mile penetration in unorganized logistics markets

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve from a transporter into an integrated logistics orchestration platform — "Everything Logistics" — combining road, rail, coastal shipping, warehousing, cold chain and supply chain solutions on a unified platform rather than selling standalone transportation
- Deepen multimodal integration through a common technology backbone, unified governance framework and customer-centric visibility systems, so services are orchestrated as one ecosystem rather than offered independently
- Technology-led transformation: accelerate deployment of AI-enabled freight control towers, predictive analytics in …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [JVs] Joint ventures are described as operating on an asset-light model, covering integrated multimodal logistics for chemicals, food grain and metals, automotive logistics focused on Japanese clients, and cold chain services for temperature-controlled warehousing and primary/secondary distribution; strategic partner shares are listed as 51%, 20% and 49%.
- [Shareholding] Promoters hold 69% as on 30th Jun'2026, with the remainder split across Indian public, foreign holdings, body corporate, mutual funds and others.
- [Market] The deck cites P/E of 14.8 and EV/EBITDA of 10.8 at 30th Jun'26, a 52-week range of Rs 1289 / Rs 868, "Stock returned CAGR of 31% in last 25 years" and "Stock coverage : 11 Buy Rating : 11".
- [Risk] Growth commentary repeatedly flags the "impact of Middle-East crises", and the Freight segment notes 24th consecutive quarter of growth alongside that impact.
- [Policy backdrop] Cited enablers include 96% of Freight Corridors operational supporting the road-to-rail shift, a logistics cost target of <=8% of GDP by 2030, ULIP crossing 160 Cr+ API transactions across 101 ICDs, and for coastal, the Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme targeting a 6% to 12% modal share by 2047.
